en: to hold; to seize; to grab

examples.en: That team finally grabbed the championship.
He worked for a long time to seize power.

examples.ko: 아이가 엄마 손을 꼭 거머쥐고 놓지 않았어요.
examples.en: The child gripped her mom's hand tightly and wouldn't let go.

examples.ko: 신인 배우가 주연상을 거머쥐어서 화제가 됐어요.
examples.en: The rookie actor won the lead acting award and became the talk of the town.
If you want to seize an opportunity, you have to prepare in advance.

examples.ko: 시장의 주도권을 거머쥔 회사가 가격을 정해요.
examples.en: The company that holds control of the market sets the prices.

explain: 손으로 꽉 잡는다는 느낌에서 '우승, 권력, 기회'처럼 큰 것을 차지한다는 뜻으로 많이 써요. 뉴스나 기사에서 자주 보이고, 일상 대화에서는 '잡다'나 '차지하다'라고 말하기도 해요.

phrases.en: He seized victory at the last moment.
phrases.nuance_ko: '승리', '우승', '권력'처럼 큰 것을 차지할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing for winning something big, such as victory or power.

phrases.en: Seize a good opportunity.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기회를 놓치지 않고 확실히 잡는다는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Gives the feeling of firmly grabbing a chance without letting go.

phrases.en: The child was clutching coins in their hand.
phrases.nuance_ko: 원래 뜻인 손으로 꽉 잡는 모습을 그대로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the original image of gripping tightly with the hand.

explain_en: It carries the feel of gripping hard with the hand, and is used for winning big things such as a title, power or a chance. You see it in news articles, while in daily talk people may say '잡다' or '차지하다'.

examples.en: Every country has its own culture.

examples.ko: 이 도시는 어디와도 다른 고유한 분위기가 있어요.
examples.en: This city has a unique atmosphere unlike anywhere else.

examples.ko: 이 춤은 이 마을에서만 전해 오는 고유한 전통이에요.
examples.en: This dance is a unique tradition handed down only in this village.
I think hanbok is clothing unique to Korea.

examples.ko: 이 이름은 우리 가문에만 고유해서 다른 가문은 안 써요.
examples.en: This name is unique to our family, so no other family uses it.
I learned that everyone's fingerprints are unique.

explain: '특별하다'는 보통과 다르다는 느낌이고, '고유하다'는 그 나라나 사람만이 원래 가진 것이라는 뜻이 강해요. 보통 '고유한 문화'처럼 명사 앞에서 쓰고 '고유의'도 자주 말해요. '독특하다'는 눈에 띄게 별나다는 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: Korea has many traditional foods of its own.
phrases.nuance_ko: '고유한'은 형용사 활용형이고, '고유의'는 '~의' 모양으로 명사 앞에 바로 붙여 써요. 뜻은 비슷해요.
phrases.nuance_en: '고유한' is the adjective form, while '고유의' attaches '의' directly before a noun. The meaning is about the same.

phrases.en: Each region has its own unique flavor.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음식이나 장소가 원래부터 가진 맛을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a flavor that a food or place has originally and only it has.

phrases.example: 이 동물은 다른 동물에게 없는 고유한 특징이 있어요.
phrases.en: This animal has unique features that other animals don't have.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그것만 가진 특징을 설명할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used to describe a feature that belongs only to that thing.

explain_en: 특별하다 means different from the usual; 고유하다 stresses that only this country or person has it originally. It usually comes before a noun ('고유한 문화'), and '고유의' is also common. 독특하다 feels noticeably odd or distinctive.

examples.en: I gave my father golf clubs for his birthday.

examples.ko: 골프채 한 세트는 값이 꽤 비싸요.
examples.en: A set of golf clubs is quite expensive.
I loaded the golf clubs, bag and all, into the car.
This golf club is light, so it is easy to use.
Holding a golf club for the first time felt awkward.
Each golf club has a different use.

explain: 운동마다 도구 이름이 달라서 야구는 '방망이', 테니스는 '라켓', 골프는 '골프채'라고 해요. 동사도 달라서 '골프를 치다', '골프채를 휘두르다'처럼 써요. 골프채 하나하나는 '드라이버', '아이언'처럼 이름이 따로 있어요.

phrases.en: My father swung the golf club hard.
phrases.nuance_ko: 치는 동작을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used for the swinging motion.

phrases.en: I bought a new set of golf clubs.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 개를 묶어서 살 때 '세트'로 세요.
phrases.nuance_en: Clubs bought together are counted as a 세트.

phrases.en: I hit the ball far with a golf club.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조사 '(으)로'를 붙여 도구로 쓴다고 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The particle (으)로 marks the club as the tool used.
phrases.en_equiv: to hit with a golf club

explain_en: Each sport names its tool differently: '방망이' for baseball, '라켓' for tennis, '골프채' for golf. The verbs differ too: '골프를 치다' and '골프채를 휘두르다'. Individual clubs have their own names, like '드라이버' and '아이언'.

examples.en: Christianity is a religion with many followers around the world.

examples.ko: 이 건물은 그리스도교 문화의 영향을 받았어요.
examples.en: This building was influenced by Christian culture.
The big holidays of Christianity are Christmas and Easter.
We learned about the history of Christianity in class.

examples.ko: 유럽 미술에는 그리스도교 이야기가 자주 나와요.
examples.en: Christian stories often appear in European art.

examples.ko: 그리스도교 신자인 친구와 성당에 가 봤어요.
examples.en: I went to a cathedral with a friend who is a Christian.

explain: 가톨릭, 개신교 등을 모두 포함해서 말할 때 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '기독교'라고 더 자주 하고, 한국에서는 '기독교'가 개신교만 가리키는 경우도 많아요. '그리스도교'는 수업이나 설명, 글에서 더 자주 보여요.

phrases.en: There are many Christians in Korea.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 뜻으로 일상 대화에서 더 자주 쓰지만, 한국에서는 개신교만 가리키기도 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same religion, more common in everyday talk, but in Korea it often means only Protestantism.

phrases.en: There are many Christians around the world.
phrases.nuance_ko: 종교를 믿는 사람을 말할 때 '그리스도교' 뒤에 '신자'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '신자' after 그리스도교 to talk about the people who believe in it.

phrases.en: Europe has a strong Christian cultural influence.
phrases.nuance_ko: 종교가 만든 생활과 전통을 설명할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for describing traditions shaped by the religion.

explain_en: It is used to cover Catholicism, Protestantism and others all together. In daily conversation '기독교' is more common, and in Korea '기독교' often refers to Protestantism only. '그리스도교' shows up more in classes, explanations and writing.

examples.ko: 이 탑은 전쟁을 기억하려고 세운 기념물이에요.
examples.en: This tower is a monument built to remember the war.

examples.ko: 공원에는 오래된 기념물이 여러 개 있어요.
examples.en: The park has several old monuments.

examples.ko: 외국 관광객들이 기념물 앞에서 사진을 찍어요.
examples.en: Foreign tourists take photos in front of the monument.
The country protects this monument.

examples.ko: 졸업 기념물로 나무를 한 그루 심었어요.
examples.en: We planted a tree as a graduation memorial.

examples.ko: 시청 앞 기념물에 사람들이 꽃을 놓았어요.
examples.en: People laid flowers at the monument in front of city hall.

explain: 큰 사건이나 사람을 기억하려고 세운 건물이나 조각을 말해요. '천연기념물'은 나라에서 보호하는 동물·식물·자연이라서 따로 외워 두세요. 여행에서 사 오는 작은 물건은 '기념품'이에요.

phrases.en: Citizens put up a monument in the square.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기념물을 만들어 세우는 행동을 말할 때 가장 자연스러운 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most natural pairing for the act of building a monument.

phrases.en: We took a photo in front of the monument.
phrases.nuance_ko: 관광지나 공원에서 장소를 말할 때 조사와 함께 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common place phrase with a particle at sights and parks.

phrases.en: On my trip I looked around the famous monuments.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여행 중에 기념물을 보러 다니는 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for visiting and looking at monuments while traveling.

explain_en: It refers to a building or statue built to remember a big event or a person. 천연기념물 is a separate term for animals, plants, and nature protected by the state. The small things you buy on trips are 기념품.

examples.en: The serialized comic has finally come out as a book.
I bought volume one of the comic at the bookstore.
We plan to gather the papers and make a book.
Books tend to cost more than magazines.

examples.ko: 도서관에서 단행본과 잡지를 따로 정리해 뒀어요.
examples.en: The library sorted the books and magazines separately.
They say they'll hold an author signing when the book comes out.

explain: 잡지나 신문, 웹에 연재된 글이 한 권의 책으로 묶여 나올 때 많이 써요. 일상 대화에서는 그냥 '책'이라고 하고, '단행본'은 출판이나 서점 이야기에서 자주 들려요.

phrases.en: The novel will be published as a book next month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 연재된 글이 책으로 나오는 일을 말할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing for a serialized work coming out as a book.

phrases.en: We plan to bind the serialized writing into a book.
phrases.nuance_ko: 흩어진 글을 한 권의 책으로 모은다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means to gather scattered writing into one book.

phrases.example: 단행본 한 권 값이 만 오천 원이에요.
phrases.en: One book costs fifteen thousand won.
phrases.nuance_ko: 책을 셀 때 '권'과 함께 써서 가격이나 수를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with the counter '권' to talk about price or number of books.

explain_en: It is often used when writing serialized in magazines, newspapers, or on the web is gathered into a single book. In daily talk people just say '책', while '단행본' is common in publishing and bookstore contexts.

dis.h: book published as its own volume, not serial

p.n: 책 is neutral and loses the sense of a standalone volume.

examples.en: We did recreation activities at the company workshop.

examples.ko: 수학여행 때 레크리에이션 시간이 제일 재미있었어요.
examples.en: The recreation time was the most fun on the school trip.
The recreation instructor led the games.
I prepared recreation activities for the children.

examples.ko: 저녁 식사 후에 레크리에이션이 있을 거예요.
examples.en: There will be group games after dinner.
Thanks to the group games, we became much closer.

explain: 한국에서 '레크리에이션'은 보통 여럿이 모여 하는 게임이나 놀이를 말해서 '레크'라고 줄여 부르기도 해요. 혼자 즐기는 취미는 '취미'나 '여가 활동'이라고 해요. 단체 행사에서 자주 들어요.

phrases.en: We did group games at the workshop.
phrases.nuance_ko: '레크리에이션'을 줄인 말로, 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A shortened form of 레크리에이션, common in speech.

phrases.example: 레크리에이션 시간에 다 같이 게임을 했어요.
phrases.en: We all played games together during recreation time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 행사 순서에서 게임이나 놀이를 하는 시간을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The part of an event schedule set aside for games and play.

phrases.en: The school held a recreation event.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여럿이 함께 즐기는 놀이 행사를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for an event where many people enjoy games together.

explain_en: In Korea '레크리에이션' usually means games and play done by a group, and is sometimes shortened to '레크'. Solo hobbies are called '취미' or '여가 활동'. You hear it often at group events.

examples.ko: 이번 달 문예지 표지가 정말 예뻐요.
examples.en: This month's literary magazine has a really pretty cover.
That poet published a poem in a literary magazine.
Literary magazines carry both poems and stories.
Old literary magazines are piled up in the library.
Some writers made their debut through literary magazines.
In our club we made a literary magazine ourselves.

explain: 시, 소설, 평론 같은 문학 작품을 싣는 잡지예요. 일반 잡지와 달리 문학 작품이 중심이라서 '계간 문예지'처럼 계절마다 나오는 것도 많아요.

phrases.example: 이 문예지는 계절마다 나오는 계간 문예지예요.
phrases.en: This literary magazine is a quarterly that comes out every season.
phrases.nuance_ko: '문예지'에 '계간'을 붙여 계절마다 나오는 잡지임을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 계간 (quarterly) to 문예지 tells you it is published every season.

phrases.en: My poem was published in a literary magazine.
phrases.nuance_ko: 작품이 잡지에 나올 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The usual phrase for a work being printed in a magazine.
phrases.en_equiv: to be published in a literary magazine

phrases.en: I read literary magazines at the library every weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문예지를 읽는 일상적인 행동을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the everyday act of reading literary magazines.

explain_en: It is a magazine that publishes literary works such as poems, fiction and criticism. Unlike general magazines it centers on literature, and many come out seasonally, like a '계간 문예지' (quarterly).

examples.en: The go board is full of stones.
My father brought out the go board.
The roads run neatly in a grid like a go board.

examples.ko: 바둑판은 가로세로 줄이 열아홉 개씩 있어요.
examples.en: A go board has nineteen lines in each direction.
I bought a checkered shirt.

examples.ko: 바둑판에서는 한 수 한 수가 중요해요.
examples.en: On the go board, every single move matters.

explain: 바둑을 두는 판이고, 가로세로로 줄이 반듯하게 그어져 있어서 격자무늬를 말할 때도 '바둑판무늬', '바둑판처럼'이라고 해요. 체스판은 '체스판'이라고 따로 불러요.

phrases.en: I bought a checkered shirt.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바둑판처럼 가로세로 줄이 있는 격자무늬를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a grid or checkered pattern like a go board.

phrases.en: The streets in this city are straight like a grid.
phrases.nuance_ko: 줄이 가로세로로 반듯한 모양을 비유할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A simile for neat, straight grid-like lines.

phrases.en: Grandfather placed a stone on the go board.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바둑을 둘 때 하는 동작을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the basic action when playing go.
phrases.en_equiv: to place a stone on the board

explain_en: It is the board on which go is played, and because it has neat lines running both ways, it is also used for grid patterns, as in '바둑판무늬' and '바둑판처럼'. A chessboard is called '체스판' separately.

examples.ko: 한 나라 안에 두 가지 언어가 병존해요.
examples.en: Two languages coexist within one country.

examples.ko: 전통과 현대가 병존하는 도시라서 구경할 곳이 많아요.
examples.en: It's a city where tradition and modernity coexist, so there's a lot to see.

examples.ko: 서로 다른 문화가 병존하려면 이해가 필요해요.
examples.en: For different cultures to coexist, understanding is needed.
Confusion arose as the two systems existed together.

examples.ko: 이 책은 과학과 종교가 병존할 수 있는지 다뤄요.
examples.en: This book deals with whether science and religion can coexist.

examples.ko: 옛 시장과 새 건물이 병존하고 있어서 독특해요.
examples.en: The old market and new buildings exist together, which is unusual.

explain: '병립하다'와 비슷하게 둘 이상이 함께 있다는 뜻으로 쓰지만, '병존하다'는 함께 존재한다는 데, '병립하다'는 나란히 서 있다는 데 초점이 있어요. 둘 다 글이나 뉴스에서 많이 보이고, 'A와 B가 병존하다'로 써요.

phrases.en: It is a village where the old and the new coexist.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤에 오는 명사를 꾸며 줄 때 쓰는 형태로, 글에서 자주 보여요.
phrases.nuance_en: A modifying form placed before a noun, common in writing.

phrases.example: 사람과 자연이 공존하는 도시를 만들고 싶어요.
phrases.en: I want to build a city where people and nature coexist.
phrases.nuance_ko: '병존하다'와 뜻이 비슷하고 더 자주 써요. 서로 다른 것이 같은 곳에서 함께 지낸다는 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar in meaning to 병존하다 but more common; it suggests different things existing together in the same place.

phrases.example: 한 건물에 가게와 사무실이 함께 있어요.
phrases.en: A shop and an office are together in one building.
phrases.nuance_ko: '병존하다'를 일상 대화에서 쉽게 말할 때 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easy everyday way to say 병존하다.

explain_en: Like '병립하다', it says two or more things exist together, but '병존하다' focuses on existing together while '병립하다' focuses on standing side by side. Both appear mostly in writing and news, in the pattern 'A와 B가 병존하다'.

examples.en: This museum has a very wide variety of items in its collection.
We lent my father's collection to the exhibition.
My most treasured item is an old stamp.

examples.ko: 미술관 소장품 중에서 이 그림이 제일 유명해요.
examples.en: Among the museum's collection, this painting is the most famous.
Part of the collection was damaged in the fire.

examples.ko: 개인 소장품이라 사진을 찍으면 안 돼요.
examples.en: It's a personal collection item, so you can't take photos.

explain: 박물관이나 미술관, 또는 개인이 가지고 보관하는 물건에 써요. '수집품'은 모은 물건이라는 점이 강하고, 소장품은 자기가 가지고 있다는 점이 강해요. '소장하다'와 같이 기억하면 좋아요.

phrases.example: 이 그림은 개인 소장품이라서 평소에는 볼 수 없어요.
phrases.en: This painting is a private collection, so you can't usually see it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 박물관이 아니라 개인이 가진 물건이라는 점을 분명히 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to make clear the items belong to an individual, not a museum.

phrases.example: 할아버지는 평생 모은 소장품을 박물관에 기증하셨어요.
phrases.en: My grandfather donated the collection he gathered over his life to a museum.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자기 물건을 박물관 등에 무료로 내놓을 때 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for giving your own items to a museum for free.

phrases.example: 이번 달에 미술관에서 소장품 전시가 열려요.
phrases.en: An exhibition of the museum's own collection is being held at the art gallery this month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 곳에서 빌려 온 작품이 아니라 그곳이 가진 작품을 보여 주는 전시를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a show of works the venue itself owns, not borrowed ones.

explain_en: It is used for items kept by a museum, an art gallery or an individual. '수집품' stresses that the things were collected, while 소장품 stresses that someone owns and holds them. It helps to learn it together with '소장하다'.

examples.ko: 저는 오래된 우표를 많이 소장하고 있어요.
examples.en: I own a lot of old stamps in my collection.
This museum holds rare paintings.
I inherited the books my father had kept.

examples.ko: 친구는 만화책 전집을 소장하고 싶어 해요.
examples.en: My friend wants to own the complete comic book set.
The library kept that letter in its collection.
It's a record worth keeping in a collection.

explain: 그냥 '갖고 있다'가 아니라 값지거나 의미 있는 물건을 모아서 오래 간직한다는 느낌이 있어요. 박물관·도서관·수집가에게 잘 어울려요. 영상이나 전자책을 사서 평생 보관하는 것도 요즘은 '소장'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: I looked at the museum's collection.
phrases.nuance_ko: '소장하다'에서 나온 명사로, 간직하고 있는 귀한 물건을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A noun from 소장하다 meaning valuable items that are kept.

phrases.en: That painting is kept at the National Museum.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건이 있는 곳을 말할 때 쓰는 피동 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A passive expression used to say where an item is kept.

phrases.en: I really want to keep this book in my collection.
phrases.nuance_ko: 좋아하는 책이나 앨범을 오래 갖고 싶을 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often said about a book or album you want to keep for good.

explain_en: Not just 'have': it implies keeping something valuable or meaningful for a long time, so it fits museums, libraries and collectors. These days buying a video or e-book to keep permanently is also called '소장'.

p.s: 그는 옛날 책을 많이 소장하고 있어요.
p.o: 그는 옛날 책을 많이 소유하고 있어요.
p.n: 소유하다 just says he owns them; 소장하다 implies he keeps them as a collection.

examples.en: You must wear goggles at the swimming pool.
My goggles keep fogging up.

examples.ko: 새 수경 하나 사러 스포츠 용품점에 갔어요.
examples.en: I went to the sports store to buy a new pair of goggles.

examples.ko: 수경에 김이 서리지 않게 닦아 주세요.
examples.en: Please wipe the goggles so they don't fog up.
I bought a small pair of goggles for my child.

examples.ko: 수경 덕분에 눈이 하나도 안 아파요.
examples.en: Thanks to the goggles, my eyes don't hurt at all.

explain: 수영할 때 눈을 보호하려고 쓰는 안경이에요. 일상에서는 '물안경'이라는 말도 많이 써요. 수영 용품을 파는 곳에서는 '수경'이라는 이름으로 쓰는 경우가 많아요.

phrases.en: I bought my child blue swimming goggles.
phrases.nuance_ko: '수경'과 같은 뜻이에요. 일상 대화에서는 '물안경'을 더 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 수경; 물안경 is more common in everyday talk.

phrases.en: I took off my goggles after swimming.
phrases.nuance_ko: '쓰다'의 반대로 쓰는 짝말이에요. 수영장에서 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The natural opposite of putting them on, common at the pool.

phrases.en: Water leaks into my goggles and my eyes sting.
phrases.nuance_ko: 수경이 얼굴에 잘 안 맞을 때 하는 말이에요. 문제를 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Said when the goggles don't fit well; used to describe a problem.

explain_en: These are the glasses you wear to protect your eyes while swimming. In daily speech people also say 물안경. Shops that sell swimming gear often label them 수경.

examples.en: Every winter I go snowboarding with my friends.
Snowboarding is harder to balance on than skiing.

examples.ko: 처음 스노보드를 배울 때 많이 넘어졌어요.
examples.en: I fell a lot when I first learned to snowboard.
How much does it cost to rent snowboard equipment?

examples.ko: 동생은 스노보드 선수가 되고 싶어 해요.
examples.en: My younger brother wants to become a snowboard athlete.

examples.ko: 주말에 초보자용 강습을 신청해서 스노보드 수업을 들어요.
examples.en: I signed up for a beginner course and take snowboard lessons on weekends.

explain: 스키도 스노보드도 동사는 '타다'를 써서 '스노보드를 타다'라고 해요. 타는 사람은 '스노보더'라고 부르고, 스키 타는 사람은 '스키어'라고 해요.

phrases.en: I want to learn snowboarding this winter.
phrases.nuance_ko: 처음 시작해서 방법을 익힐 때는 '타다' 대신 '배우다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '배우다' instead of '타다' when you are just starting and learning how.

phrases.en: The snowboarder comes down the snow quickly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 스노보드를 타는 사람을 가리키는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the word for a person who snowboards.

phrases.example: 스노보드 장비는 가게에서 빌릴 수 있어요.
phrases.en: You can rent snowboard equipment at the shop.
phrases.nuance_ko: 보드와 부츠처럼 타는 데 필요한 물건을 묶어서 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: This groups together the things you need to ride, like the board and boots.

explain_en: Both skiing and snowboarding use the verb 타다, so you say 스노보드를 타다. A person who snowboards is a 스노보더, and a person who skis is a 스키어.

examples.en: I rode a skateboard in the park on the weekend.
My younger brother got a skateboard as a birthday present.
Balancing on a skateboard is hard at first.

examples.ko: 저 아이는 스케이트보드를 아주 잘 타요.
examples.en: That kid is really good at skateboarding.

examples.ko: 스케이트보드를 탈 때는 헬멧을 꼭 써야 해요.
examples.en: You must wear a helmet when you ride a skateboard.

examples.ko: 길에서 스케이트보드를 타면 위험할 수 있어요.
examples.en: Riding a skateboard on the street can be dangerous.

explain: '스케이트보드'는 바퀴가 달린 판 위에 서서 타는 놀이 기구예요. 손잡이가 달린 '킥보드'와 달라요. 눈 위에서 타는 '스노보드'와도 헷갈리지 마세요. '스케이트보드를 타다'로 말해요.

phrases.example: 저는 다음 달부터 스케이트보드를 배울 거예요.
phrases.en: I'm going to learn skateboarding starting next month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 새로 타는 법을 익힐 때 써요. 동사 '타다' 대신 '배우다'를 쓴 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when learning to ride. It uses 배우다 instead of 타다.

phrases.example: 그 친구는 스케이트보드 선수가 되고 싶어 해요.
phrases.en: That friend wants to become a skateboarder.
phrases.nuance_ko: 스케이트보드를 전문으로 타는 사람이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Someone who skateboards professionally.

phrases.en: I go to school on a skateboard.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조사 '-로'를 붙여 이동 수단을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The particle -로 is attached to name the means of transport.

explain_en: '스케이트보드' is a wheeled board you stand on and ride. It differs from a '킥보드', which has a handle, and from a '스노보드', which is ridden on snow. You say '스케이트보드를 타다'.

examples.en: The World Cup winning team held a parade downtown.

examples.ko: 시가행진 때문에 오늘 길이 많이 막혀요.
examples.en: The roads are very jammed today because of the parade.
A parade is held on the last day of the festival.
The children gathered by the road to watch the parade.
The students in the parade waved flags.
Cars can't enter the parade route.

explain: 축하나 기념 행사로 사람들이 거리를 줄지어 걷는 것을 말해요. '퍼레이드'와 비슷한 상황에 쓰지만, 시가행진은 한자어라서 뉴스나 공지에서 더 어울려요. '시가행진을 하다/벌이다'로 많이 써요.

phrases.en: Citizens held a parade in the streets.
phrases.nuance_ko: 많은 사람이 모여 행진할 때 '벌이다'를 써서 행사의 규모를 보여 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: 벌이다 conveys the large scale of the event when many people gather to march.

phrases.example: 시가행진 구간에는 차가 다닐 수 없어요.
phrases.en: Cars cannot pass along the parade route.
phrases.nuance_ko: 행진이 지나가는 길을 가리킬 때 공지나 뉴스에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in notices and news to refer to the stretch of road a parade passes.

phrases.en: There is a parade on the last day of the festival.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻은 비슷하지만 일상 대화에서는 외래어 '퍼레이드'가 더 편해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar in meaning, but the loanword is more casual in everyday speech.

explain_en: It means people moving in a line through the streets for a celebration or commemoration. It describes much the same scene as '퍼레이드', but as a Sino-Korean word it suits news and notices better. It is commonly used as '시가행진을 하다/벌이다'.

examples.en: I looked around an old temple in Greece.

examples.ko: 언덕 위에 하얀 신전이 서 있어요.
examples.en: A white temple stands on the hill.

examples.ko: 이 신전은 이천 년 전에 지어졌어요.
examples.en: This temple was built two thousand years ago.
People made wishes in front of the temple.

examples.ko: 게임 속 신전에는 보물이 숨겨져 있어요.
examples.en: There is hidden treasure in the temple in the game.

examples.ko: 신전의 기둥이 아직도 튼튼하게 남아 있어요.
examples.en: The temple's pillars still stand strong.

explain: 신을 모시는 큰 건물을 말할 때 써요. 한국의 절은 '절', 교회는 '교회'라고 하고 '신전'은 그리스, 이집트처럼 고대 문명이나 판타지 게임에서 주로 나와요. 한국 전통 건물에는 거의 쓰지 않아요.

phrases.example: 옛날 사람들은 신을 위해 큰 신전을 지었어요.
phrases.en: People in the old days built a big temple for their gods.
phrases.nuance_ko: 고대 이야기에서 '신전'과 가장 잘 어울리는 동사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb that most naturally goes with 신전 in stories about ancient times.

phrases.en: I'll show you a photo of a Greek temple.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나라 이름과 함께 써서 어느 문명의 신전인지 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Paired with a country name to say which civilization's temple it is.

phrases.en: The temple's pillars are very tall.
phrases.nuance_ko: '의'를 붙여 신전의 일부를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses 의 to talk about a part of the temple.

explain_en: Used for large buildings of ancient religions. Korean temples are called '절' and churches '교회'; '신전' appears for Greece, Egypt or fantasy games, and is rarely used for Korean traditional buildings.

examples.ko: 이 학교에는 작은 현악 앙상블이 있어요.
examples.en: This school has a small string ensemble.
The ensemble of piano and violin was truly beautiful.

examples.ko: 네 사람의 앙상블 덕분에 공연이 완벽했어요.
examples.en: Thanks to the four people's ensemble, the performance was perfect.

examples.ko: 배우들의 앙상블 연기가 좋아서 영화가 재미있어요.
examples.en: The film is fun because the actors work so well together.
We practice every day to get in sync as an ensemble.

examples.ko: 공연이 끝나자 앙상블 단원들이 인사를 했어요.
examples.en: When the show ended, the ensemble members bowed.

explain: 음악에서는 여럿이 함께 연주하는 팀이나 그 호흡을 말하고, 영화나 연극에서는 배우들이 서로 잘 맞는 연기를 말해요. 프랑스어에서 온 외래어라서 '합주'나 '조화'로 바꿔 쓸 때도 있어요.

phrases.en: The two actors made a wonderful ensemble.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여럿이 서로 잘 어울릴 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for when several people fit well together.

phrases.en: This team works together really well.
phrases.nuance_ko: 호흡이 잘 맞는다는 칭찬으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A compliment meaning the members are in good sync.

phrases.example: 우리 반은 오늘 합주 연습을 했어요.
phrases.en: Our class practiced playing together today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음악에서 '앙상블'을 우리말로 바꿔 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: A native-word replacement for 앙상블 in music.

explain_en: In music it means a group playing together or their sense of timing, and in film or theater it means actors who play well off each other. It is a loanword from French, and '합주' or '조화' can sometimes replace it.

en: to love; to like; to be fond of

examples.en: My grandfather is very fond of traditional tea.

examples.ko: 많은 사람이 이 브랜드의 제품을 애호해요.
examples.en: Many people love this brand's products.
I have been fond of classical music for a long time.
That writer is a novelist loved by readers.

examples.ko: 제가 애호하는 가게는 골목 끝에 있어요.
examples.en: The shop I love going to is at the end of the alley.

examples.ko: 저는 단 음식을 별로 애호하지 않아요.
examples.en: I'm not very fond of sweet food.

explain: '좋아하다'보다 격식 있고, 오랫동안 꾸준히 즐기고 아끼는 느낌이에요. 같은 취미를 즐기는 사람을 '애호가'라고 하는데, 이 말과 함께 알아 두면 좋아요.

phrases.en: He is a longtime jazz lover.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 것을 오래 즐기고 아끼는 사람을 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A word for someone who has long enjoyed and cherished something.

phrases.example: 제가 애호하는 작가가 새 책을 냈어요.
phrases.en: A writer I love has published a new book.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸미는 모양이에요. 오래 아끼는 대상에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The form that modifies a noun, used for something one has cherished for a long time.

phrases.en: I like warm tea.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻이 비슷하고 일상 대화에서 훨씬 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar in meaning and far more natural in daily conversation.

explain_en: It is more formal than '좋아하다' and suggests enjoying and cherishing something steadily over a long time. A person who enjoys a hobby this way is called an '애호가' (enthusiast), which is worth learning together.

dis.h: formal: love a hobby or interest

p.n: 사랑하다 is a stronger, more emotional love. 애호하다 means being a fond fan of something.

examples.en: An international expo was held in Yeosu.
The subway is crowded during the expo.
I looked at new books at a book expo.
I bought expo tickets in advance.
The theme of this expo is the environment.

examples.ko: 엑스포를 보러 외국인 관광객이 많이 와요.
examples.en: Many foreign tourists come to see the expo.

explain: 엑스포는 큰 국제 행사나 산업 전시 이름에 주로 붙고, 작은 행사에는 '박람회'나 '전시회'를 많이 써요. '대전 엑스포', '푸드 엑스포'처럼 이름 뒤에 붙는 경우도 흔해요.

phrases.en: This year our city is holding an expo.
phrases.nuance_ko: 행사를 여는 쪽에서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used from the side of the organizer holding the event.

phrases.en: I will go to the expo with my family on the weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 구경하러 가는 사람의 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: What a visitor would say.

phrases.example: 엑스포 개막 날에는 사람이 정말 많았어요.
phrases.en: On the opening day of the expo, there were so many people.
phrases.nuance_ko: 행사가 시작되는 때를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the time the event starts.

explain_en: 엑스포 mostly appears in the names of large international events or industry shows, while smaller events are usually called 박람회 or 전시회. It is also common as a name tag, as in 대전 엑스포 or 푸드 엑스포.

examples.en: That director is very famous in the film world.
The film industry is going through hard times these days.
I'm studying acting to get into the film world.
People from the film world gathered at the awards ceremony.
Young directors in the film world are getting attention.
He left the film world and became a novelist.

explain: '-계'는 어떤 분야의 사람들과 세계를 묶어 부르는 말이에요. '연예계', '정치계', '학계'처럼 쓰고, '영화계'는 감독, 배우, 제작사까지 영화와 관련된 사람들 전체를 말해요.

phrases.en: I saw news about the film world on the news.
phrases.nuance_ko: 영화 분야의 소식을 말할 때 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for news about the film field.

phrases.en: People from the film world gathered at the awards ceremony.
phrases.nuance_ko: 감독, 배우 같은 영화 관련 사람들을 묶어 부를 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Groups together directors, actors, and others in film.

phrases.en: After graduating, I entered the film industry.
phrases.nuance_ko: 영화 분야에서 일을 시작한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means starting to work in the film field.

explain_en: '-계' groups the people and world of a field together, as in '연예계', '정치계' and '학계'. '영화계' covers everyone connected to film, including directors, actors and producers.

en: to be colorful; to be multicolored; to be many-hued

examples.en: Fireworks decorated the night sky in dazzling colors.
Brilliantly colored hanbok were hanging in the market.
The Christmas tree is so colorful it dazzles my eyes.
I walked through a field of multicolored flowers.
The stage lights changed into a rainbow of colors.
The autumn mountains are a blaze of color because of the leaves.

explain: 여러 가지 색이 화려하게 어우러진 모습에 써요. '알록달록'은 귀엽고 가벼운 느낌이고, '오색찬란'은 더 화려하고 멋진 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: The Christmas streets are full of dazzling, many-colored lights.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에 붙여 화려한 색을 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Placed before a noun to describe splendid colors.

phrases.en: The mountain in autumn colors is truly splendid.
phrases.nuance_ko: 풍경이 여러 색으로 화려할 때 해요체로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Polite style for scenery shining in many colors.

phrases.en: The child is holding a colorful umbrella.
phrases.nuance_ko: '오색찬란'보다 쉽고 귀엽고 가벼운 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Easier and lighter, with a cuter feel than the headword.

explain_en: It describes many colors blending in a splendid way. '알록달록' feels cute and light, while '오색찬란' feels more gorgeous and grand.

examples.en: Grandma keeps kimchi in an earthenware jar.
An onggi jar is a vessel that breathes.
I bought a small earthenware pot at the market.
Bowls made of earthenware are heavy but sturdy.

examples.ko: 옹기 마을에서 직접 항아리를 빚어 봤어요.
examples.en: I shaped a jar myself in the pottery village.
Earthenware jars are lined up on the jangdokdae.

explain: 된장, 간장, 김치를 담는 갈색 항아리가 대표적이에요. '도자기'는 높은 온도에서 구운 매끈한 그릇이고, '옹기'는 숨구멍이 있어서 발효 음식을 두기에 좋다고 해요.

phrases.en: Food keeps longer when stored in earthenware.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옹기로 만든 그릇을 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A name for vessels made of onggi earthenware.

phrases.en: I stored the soybean paste in an earthenware jar.
phrases.nuance_ko: 발효 음식을 보관할 때 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common phrase for storing fermented foods.

phrases.en: Earthenware jars are lined up in the yard.
phrases.nuance_ko: 간장, 된장을 담는 큰 항아리를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the large jars that hold soy sauce or soybean paste.

explain_en: The typical example is the brown jar for 된장, 간장 and 김치. 도자기 is smooth, high-fired ware, whereas 옹기 is porous and said to be good for fermented food.

examples.en: The couple danced a waltz at their wedding.

examples.ko: 왈츠 음악이 나오자 사람들이 짝을 지었어요.
examples.en: When waltz music started, people paired up.

examples.ko: 왈츠 스텝이 어려워서 매일 연습하고 있어요.
examples.en: The waltz steps are hard, so I practice every day.
We turned slowly to an elegant waltz.
The first dance I learned was the waltz.
A slow waltz is playing on the radio.

explain: '왈츠'는 3박자 춤이라 '하나, 둘, 셋' 하고 세는 느낌으로 춰요. 동사는 '추다'를 쓰고 '왈츠를 추다'처럼 같이 말해요. '탱고', '블루스'처럼 서양 춤 이름은 대부분 외래어 그대로 써요.

phrases.en: We danced a waltz at the party.
phrases.nuance_ko: 춤 이름에는 동사 '추다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Dance names take the verb 추다.

phrases.en: I'm learning the waltz these days.
phrases.nuance_ko: 춤을 익히는 중이라고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you are learning the dance.

phrases.en: This waltz piece is very smooth.
phrases.nuance_ko: 왈츠에 맞는 음악을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to music written for a waltz.

explain_en: The '왈츠' is in three beats, danced with a feel of counting one-two-three. The verb is '추다', as in '왈츠를 추다'. Western dance names such as '탱고' and '블루스' are mostly used as loanwords.

en: to enter into an organization; to join an organization

examples.en: I joined a choir when I was in college.

examples.ko: 동생은 축구 클럽에 입단하려고 연습 중이에요.
examples.en: My younger sibling is practicing to join a soccer club.

examples.ko: 연습생으로 입단한 지 벌써 삼 년이 됐어요.
examples.en: It's already been three years since I joined as a trainee.

examples.ko: 신인 선수가 프로팀에 입단하면 계약금을 받기도 해요.
examples.en: When a rookie joins a pro team, he sometimes receives a signing bonus.

examples.ko: 어느 극단에 입단할지 아직 고민 중이에요.
examples.en: I'm still deciding which theater troupe to join.

examples.ko: 입단하기 전에 간단한 시험을 봐야 해요.
examples.en: You have to take a simple test before joining.

explain: '팀에 입단하다'처럼 조사 '에'와 함께 써요. 회사에 들어가는 건 '입사하다', 학교는 '입학하다'라서 팀, 극단, 합창단 같은 곳에만 어울려요.

phrases.en: I want to join the baseball team too.
phrases.nuance_ko: 들어가고 싶은 바람을 말할 때 쓰는 활용이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A form used to express a wish to join.

phrases.en: My younger sibling ended up joining the theater troupe.
phrases.nuance_ko: 결과적으로 들어가게 되었다는 느낌을 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: Gives the sense that someone came to join as a result.

phrases.en: After joining, I practice every day.
phrases.nuance_ko: 들어간 다음의 일을 이어서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to continue talking about what happens after joining.

explain_en: It takes the particle '에', as in '팀에 입단하다'. Joining a company is '입사하다' and a school is '입학하다', so this verb fits only places like teams, troupes and choirs.

examples.ko: 이 도서관은 장서가 오십만 권이 넘어요.
examples.en: This library has a collection of more than five hundred thousand books.
Most of my grandfather's book collection is made up of old books.
Shall we search the university library's holdings?

examples.ko: 그분은 평생 모은 장서 전부를 마을 도서관에 기증했어요.
examples.en: He donated his entire lifelong book collection to the town library.

examples.ko: 이 대학의 장서에는 희귀한 고서도 많아요.
examples.en: This university's collection also includes many rare old books.

examples.ko: 장서 점검 때문에 오늘은 도서관이 일찍 문을 닫아요.
examples.en: The library closes early today because of the book inventory check.

explain: 도서관이나 개인이 가지고 있는 책 전체를 가리켜요. '장서가 많다', '장서 수'처럼 쓰고, 책 한 권을 말할 때는 그냥 '책'이라고 해요. '소장 도서'와 비슷하게 쓰는 말이에요.

phrases.en: This library has a rich collection of books.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가지고 있는 책의 수와 종류가 많다는 칭찬이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A compliment that the number and variety of books held is large.

phrases.en: My grandfather donated his book collection to the university.
phrases.nuance_ko: 개인이 모은 책 전체를 다른 곳에 준다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means giving one's whole book collection to another place.

phrases.en: I search the library's holdings.
phrases.nuance_ko: '장서'와 비슷하게 갖고 있는 책을 말해요. 도서관 검색에서 자주 보여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Like 장서, it means books held; often seen in library searches.

explain_en: It refers to the whole set of books held by a library or a person. People say '장서가 많다' or '장서 수', and for a single book you just say '책'. It is used much like '소장 도서' (books in a collection).

examples.en: My mother is preparing the food to put on the ancestral rites table.

examples.ko: 제사상이 너무 커서 상을 두 개 붙였어요.
examples.en: The ritual table was so big that we put two tables together.

examples.ko: 제사상은 집안마다 차리는 방법이 조금씩 달라요.
examples.en: How the ritual table is set differs a little from family to family.

examples.ko: 큰집에서 제사상을 차리고 모두 절을 했어요.
examples.en: At my uncle's house we set the ritual table and everyone bowed.
In front of the ritual table, the family members bow one by one.

examples.ko: 제사상까지 다 차리고 나니 밤이 되었어요.
examples.en: By the time we finished setting even the ritual table, it was night.

explain: 조상에게 제사를 지낼 때 음식을 차려 놓는 상이에요. '상을 차리다'처럼 '제사상을 차리다'라고 말해요. 설이나 추석 아침에 지내는 제사는 '차례'라고 해서 일반 '제사'와 구분하기도 해요.

phrases.en: We set the ritual table at Grandmother's house.
phrases.nuance_ko: '상을 차리다'와 같은 말로, 제사 음식을 올려 놓는 일이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Like 상을 차리다, it means laying out the food for the ritual.

phrases.en: We put fruit and rice cakes on the ritual table.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 음식을 제사상에 놓는다는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means placing certain food on the ritual table.
phrases.en_equiv: to put on the ritual table

phrases.example: 우리 집은 일 년에 두 번 제사를 지내요.
phrases.en: My family holds ancestral rites twice a year.
phrases.nuance_ko: '제사상'과 함께 알아 두면 좋은, 제사를 하는 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: It is the action of holding the rite, useful to learn with 제사상.

explain_en: It is the table where food is laid out when holding rites for ancestors. You say '제사상을 차리다', like '상을 차리다'. The rites held on the morning of Seollal or Chuseok are called '차례', which is sometimes distinguished from a regular '제사'.

en: to transmit; to re-broadcast; to diffuse

examples.en: The broadcasting station aired the final live.
This channel will broadcast tomorrow's game live.
I can hear the voice broadcasting soccer live on the radio.

examples.ko: 행사를 온라인으로 중계방송해서 많은 사람이 봤어요.
examples.en: They broadcast the event live online, so many people watched.

examples.ko: 비 때문에 중계방송할 수 없다는 공지가 떴어요.
examples.en: A notice appeared saying they could not broadcast live because of the rain.
The announcer who broadcast the Olympics live gave an interview.

explain: '방송하다'보다 구체적으로, 지금 벌어지는 일을 바로 전한다는 느낌이에요. 줄여서 '중계하다', 실시간이면 '생중계하다'라고 해요. 주로 스포츠와 큰 행사에 써요.

phrases.en: This channel broadcasts the final.
phrases.nuance_ko: '중계방송하다'의 줄임말이에요. 말할 때 더 흔해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A short form of '중계방송하다', more common in speech.

phrases.en: They will broadcast the concert live this evening.
phrases.nuance_ko: 실시간이라는 점을 더 강조해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Puts more stress on it being real time.
phrases.en_equiv: to broadcast live in real time

phrases.en: The broadcaster is airing the game right now.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 진행 중일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when it's happening right now.

explain_en: It is more specific than 방송하다: it carries the feeling of sending out what is happening right now. It is shortened to 중계하다, and 생중계하다 when it is real-time. It is mostly used for sports and big events.

examples.ko: 그 작가의 이름은 출판계에서 익히 알려져 있어요.
examples.en: That author's name is well known in the publishing world.
I often hear that the publishing industry is struggling.
People from the publishing world gathered at the book fair.
This year's talk of the publishing world is this novel.

examples.ko: 출판계는 요즘 전자책 시장에 관심이 많아요.
examples.en: The publishing world is very interested in the e-book market these days.
After graduating, I want to enter the publishing world.

explain: '-계'는 그 분야에서 일하는 사람들과 분위기 전체를 가리켜요. '연예계', '정치계', '체육계'도 같은 식이에요. 한 회사를 말하는 '출판사'와는 달리 업계 전체를 말해요.

phrases.en: I worked in the publishing industry for ten years.
phrases.nuance_ko: 출판계와 거의 같은 뜻이고, 사업 분야라는 느낌이 조금 더 강해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Nearly the same as 출판계, with a slightly stronger business feel.

phrases.en: My older sister works in the publishing world.
phrases.nuance_ko: 직업을 말할 때 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when talking about someone's job field.

phrases.en: I saw news about the publishing world on the news.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그 분야의 소식을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for news from that field.

explain_en: The suffix '-계' refers to all the people and the overall scene of a field, as in '연예계', '정치계' and '체육계'. Unlike '출판사', which is one company, 출판계 means the whole industry.

examples.en: The drum is a typical percussion instrument.
I learned percussion when I was little.
The percussion sound in this piece is impressive.
In an orchestra, the percussion sits at the back.
Drums and gongs are also percussion instruments.
The percussionist came up on stage.

explain: 치거나 두드리거나 흔들어서 소리를 내는 악기를 묶어 부르는 말이에요. 현악기, 관악기와 함께 악기를 나누는 큰 갈래예요. 꽹과리, 북, 장구 같은 전통 악기도 타악기예요.

phrases.en: I heard a percussion performance at the show yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: '타악기'로 하는 연주를 말할 때 붙여서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when talking about playing percussion instruments.

phrases.en: I play percussion every weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 두드려서 소리를 내는 악기라서 '치다'와 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: '치다' (to hit) fits because these instruments are struck.

phrases.en: The percussion sound was so loud that my heart pounded.
phrases.nuance_ko: 타악기에서 나는 소리를 말할 때 '소리' 앞에 붙여서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Placed before '소리' to refer to the sound made by percussion instruments.

explain_en: This groups instruments that make sound when struck, tapped or shaken. It is one of the main categories alongside string and wind instruments. Traditional instruments like the kkwaenggwari, buk and janggu are percussion too.

examples.en: In this performance, the pianist plays together with the orchestra.

examples.ko: 두 가수가 처음으로 협연한 무대가 화제가 됐어요.
examples.en: The stage where the two singers performed together for the first time became a hot topic.

examples.ko: 어릴 때부터 유명한 지휘자와 협연하고 싶었어요.
examples.en: Since I was young, I wanted to perform with a famous conductor.

examples.ko: 협연하는 동안 서로 눈빛을 맞추며 호흡을 확인했어요.
examples.en: While performing together, they made eye contact and checked their timing.

examples.ko: 그 두 사람은 이번 가을에 협연하기로 했어요.
examples.en: Those two decided to perform together this fall.
I'm so nervous because I'm going to perform together with my teacher.

explain: '오케스트라와 협연하다'처럼 '~와/과'와 함께 쓰는 일이 많아요. 클래식뿐 아니라 가수끼리 함께 무대에 설 때도 쓰고, 일상에서는 '같이 공연하다'라고도 해요.

phrases.example: 두 가수가 이번 축제에서 같이 공연해요.
phrases.en: The two singers will perform together at this festival.
phrases.nuance_ko: '협연하다'와 비슷한 뜻으로, 일상 대화에서 더 쉽게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 협연하다 and easier to say in daily conversation.

phrases.en: He ended up performing with a famous orchestra.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-게 되다'를 붙여 기회가 생겼다는 느낌을 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '-게 되다' it gives the sense that the chance came about.

phrases.en: I also want to perform with an orchestra someday.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-고 싶다'를 붙여 바라는 마음을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '-고 싶다' it expresses a wish.

explain_en: It is often used with '~와/과', as in '오케스트라와 협연하다'. It is used not only in classical music but also when singers share a stage, and in daily life people also say '같이 공연하다'.

en: photo spread; pictorial; collection of pictures

examples.en: That actor did a magazine photo shoot.
The new album's photo set was released today.
I made plans while looking at a travel photo book.

examples.ko: 화보 촬영 때문에 일찍 일어나야 해요.
examples.en: I have to get up early for the photo shoot.
I booked a session to shoot wedding photos.

examples.ko: 화보 속 모습이 실제와 달라서 놀랐어요.
examples.en: I was surprised that the person in the photo spread looks different in real life.

explain: 잡지나 책에서 사진을 중심으로 꾸민 쪽이나 사진 모음을 가리켜요. 연예인 이야기에서 '화보 촬영', '화보 공개'가 정말 자주 나와요. 일반 '사진'보다 콘셉트와 연출이 있는 사진 작업이라는 느낌이 강해요.

phrases.en: I have a photo shoot today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 잡지나 광고에 쓸 사진을 찍는 일을 말할 때 가장 흔하게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common phrase for shooting photos for a magazine or campaign.

phrases.en: The actor released a new photo spread.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스에서 연예인 사진이 처음 나올 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used in news when a celebrity's photos are first revealed.

phrases.example: 이번 달 잡지 화보가 정말 멋져요.
phrases.en: This month's magazine photo spread is really cool.
phrases.nuance_ko: 잡지에 실린 사진 모음을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a set of pictures printed in a magazine.

explain_en: Pages or a collection built around photographs in a magazine or book. In celebrity news, '화보 촬영' (photo shoot) and '화보 공개' (photo set release) appear constantly. Compared with a plain '사진', it suggests a styled, concept-driven photo project.
